text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- High Court okays physical pressure on Islamic Jihad man.
- Journalists accused by leader of union workers in Prime Minister Netanyahu's office of offering bribes for "dirt" on Israel's first family.
- Shin Bet secret police arrest member of suicide attacker gang; High Court allows force to be used in interrogation.
- Defence Minister Mordechai orders increase of forces in Hebron.
- Shin Bet increases guard on Netanyahu in wake of threats.
- Social security institute says 738,000 poor in 1995, among them 329,000 children.
- Clinton in letter to Syrian President Assad sent to thank Assad for his welcome of Clinton's re-election: I will act to prevent possibility of war.
- Majority of government for Hebron deal; settlers to protest.
- Message from Israeli detained in Egypt: I feel okay.
- Mordechai says army will redeploy in Hebron in orderly fashion, in light of day.
- Interview with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak: If it weren't for the publicity we'd have said take the spy.
- Globes survey: 65 percent would prefer tax rise to cut in services.
